lead: No supplement has strong evidence in Long COVID. The largest placebo-controlled supplement trial, in 463 people over 6 months, found that a probiotic and prebiotic (synbiotic) mix relieved fatigue, memory and concentration problems more often than placebo (grade B), and an 80-person trial found less fatigue and anxiety with high-dose vitamin D (grade B). Coenzyme Q10, nicotinamide riboside (an NAD+ precursor) and a B-vitamin combination did no better than placebo (grade: Negative), and no Long COVID studies testing benfotiamine or nattokinase on their own were found (grade: Insufficient).

grade_key.A: Meta-analysis, or at least 2 randomized trials with low risk of bias and a consistent benefit
grade_key.B: 1 good randomized trial, or several randomized trials with mixed results
grade_key.C: Observational studies, small pilots or open-label trials only
grade_key.Negative: Randomized trials found no benefit over placebo

disclaimer: This page summarizes published research. It is not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before starting any supplement, especially if you take other medicines.

products.name: Palmitoylethanolamide with luteolin (for loss of smell)
products.summary: For loss of smell lasting more than 6 months after COVID-19, a multicentre double-blind randomized trial in 185 people compared this supplement plus smell training with placebo plus smell training for 90 days. Smell test scores improved more with the supplement: 92% of the supplement group improved against 42% of the placebo group. It was tested only for smell loss, not for other Long COVID symptoms.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA)
general_safety.short: Trial data up to 49 days argue against serious reactions at 1 in 200 or more; generally well tolerated, but long-term data and side-effect reporting are limited.

citations.label: Di Stadio et al., 2022, Curr Neuropharmacol
citations.title: Ultramicronized Palmitoylethanolamide and Luteolin Supplement Combined with Olfactory Training to Treat Post-COVID-19 Olfactory Impairment: A Multi-Center Double-Blinded Randomized Placebo- Controlled Clinical Trial.

products.name: Probiotics and synbiotics
products.summary: In the largest trial, 463 people with Long COVID were randomized to a synbiotic preparation (a probiotic and prebiotic mix) or placebo for 6 months; more people in the synbiotic group had relief of fatigue, memory loss, difficulty concentrating, gut upset and general unwellness. Smaller placebo-controlled trials of other probiotic products, in 26 to 62 people, reported benefits on some outcomes, such as post-exercise malaise, breathing difficulty, or anxiety and depression scores, but not on others. A 14-day trial in 200 people reported less fatigue with a combined enzyme and probiotic supplement, so the effect of the probiotic alone cannot be separated. A 2024 living systematic review found no compelling evidence for combined probiotics and prebiotics. Each trial tested a different product.
products.safety_interactions: In the largest trial, adverse event rates were similar with the synbiotic and placebo. A smaller trial described its heat-treated probiotic as well tolerated, and the enzyme and probiotic trial reported no adverse events. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Probiotics
general_safety.short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.

products.name: Vitamin D
products.summary: In an 8-week double-blind randomized trial in 80 people with post-COVID fatigue or neuropsychiatric symptoms, weekly high-dose vitamin D (60,000 IU) was compared with placebo. Fatigue, anxiety and a cognitive test score improved more with vitamin D; sleep, depression, other cognitive tests and inflammation markers did not differ.
products.safety_interactions: In that trial, adverse events were about as common with vitamin D as with placebo, and no serious adverse events were reported. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Vitamin D
general_safety.short: Long-term supplementation raised the risk of high blood calcium and high urine calcium in trials, but not kidney stones; toxicity from extremely high doses is rare but serious.

citations.label: Charoenporn et al., 2024, Psychiatry Clin Neurosci
citations.title: Effects of an 8-week high-dose vitamin D supplementation on fatigue and neuropsychiatric manifestations in post-COVID syndrome: A randomized controlled trial.

products.name: Creatine
products.summary: Two small randomized trials compared creatine with placebo. In a 6-month double-blind trial in 12 people with post-COVID fatigue, 4 g a day raised creatine levels in muscle and brain compared with placebo; fatigue fell compared with the start of the trial, which is not a comparison with placebo. In a 4-week single-blind pilot trial in 67 people, combined with physical activity, fatigue and grip strength improved more with 6 g a day than with placebo; the abstract does not report the same benefit for the 18 g a day group.
products.safety_interactions: In the 4-week trial, adverse events were minimal and short-lived and did not need medical treatment. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Creatine
general_safety.short: Creatine is associated with a small rise in blood creatinine, described as transient, without a significant change in kidney filtration; no serious adverse outcomes in studies of women.

citations.label: Slankamenac et al., 2023, Food Sci Nutr
citations.title: Effects of six-month creatine supplementation on patient- and clinician-reported outcomes, and tissue creatine levels in patients with post-COVID-19 fatigue syndrome.

citations.label: Dos Santos et al., 2026, Front Nutr
citations.title: Creatine supplementation on fatigue related to post-COVID-19 condition-fatigue study: a randomized controlled trial.

products.name: L-arginine with vitamin C
products.summary: In a 28-day single-blind trial, 50 adults with Long COVID and persistent fatigue were randomized to L-arginine (1.66 g) with liposomal vitamin C (500 mg) twice a day, or placebo; 46 completed it. The supplement group walked further in 6 minutes, had better handgrip strength and blood-vessel function, and fewer reported fatigue. A secondary analysis found higher blood L-arginine levels. The trial was small, short and not double-blind, and a 2024 living systematic review found no compelling evidence for this combination.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: L-arginine
general_safety.short: Lowers blood pressure (about 6 mmHg systolic in a meta-analysis); short-term use may cause gastrointestinal and cardiovascular adverse effects.

citations.title: Effects of l-Arginine Plus Vitamin C Supplementation on Physical Performance, Endothelial Function, and Persistent Fatigue in Adults with Long COVID: A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.

citations.label: Calvani et al., 2023, Int J Mol Sci
citations.title: Effects of l-Arginine Plus Vitamin C Supplementation on l-Arginine Metabolism in Adults with Long COVID: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

citations.label: Zeraatkar et al., 2024, BMJ
citations.title: Interventions for the management of long covid (post-covid condition): living systematic review.

products.name: Oxaloacetate
products.summary: In an open-label, non-randomized 6-week study, 43 people with Long COVID and 76 with ME/CFS took oxaloacetate; there was no concurrent placebo group, and results were compared with placebo results from an earlier, separate trial. Fatigue scores fell from baseline by up to 46.8% in the Long COVID group.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Oxaloacetate
general_safety.short: Small trials of 1 to 3 months in Alzheimer's disease and ME/CFS found oxaloacetate safe and well tolerated at the doses tested.

citations.label: Cash et al., 2022, J Transl Med
citations.title: Oxaloacetate Treatment For Mental And Physical Fatigue In Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Long-COVID fatigue patients: a non-randomized controlled clinical trial.

products.name: B vitamins (B1, B6 and B12)
products.summary: In a double-blind trial in Germany, 323 people with Long COVID were randomized to 28 days of prednisolone, a combination of thiamine (vitamin B1, 100 mg), vitamin B6 and vitamin B12, both, or placebo. The B vitamins made no statistically significant or clinically meaningful difference to overall symptom severity.
products.safety_interactions: Adverse events were evenly spread between the groups, with no serious adverse events related to the study treatments. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: B vitamins
general_safety.short: High vitamin B6 levels, usually from supplements, may cause sensory nerve damage. Folic acid did not change cancer rates over about 5 years in large trials.

citations.label: Gágyor et al., 2026, EClinicalMedicine
citations.title: Low-dose prednisolone and B vitamins for post-COVID-19 syndrome in Germany: the PreVitaCOV randomised clinical trial.

products.name: Beetroot juice
products.summary: In a 14-day double-blind pilot randomized trial in adults with Long COVID, 25 of 31 participants completed beetroot juice or a placebo drink. Fatigue resistance and walking distance improved from baseline in both groups, with no difference between them; gut bacteria and some inflammatory markers changed with beetroot juice. This is a single small pilot trial.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Beetroot juice and dietary nitrate
general_safety.short: No serious adverse events in a 12-week trial in older adults; a review warns beetroot juice can push nitrate intake above the acceptable daily intake.

citations.label: Calvani et al., 2024, Clin Nutr
citations.title: Beetroot juice intake positively influenced gut microbiota and inflammation but failed to improve functional outcomes in adults with long COVID: A pilot randomized controlled trial.

products.name: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10)
products.summary: In a double-blind crossover trial, 121 people with Long COVID were randomized to take 500 mg of CoQ10 a day or placebo for 6 weeks each, and 119 completed both periods. CoQ10 did not reduce the number or severity of Long COVID symptoms compared with placebo; symptoms improved over time in both periods regardless of treatment. A 2024 living systematic review also found no compelling evidence for CoQ10.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.

citations.label: Hansen et al., 2023, Lancet Reg Health Eur
citations.title: High-dose coenzyme Q10 therapy versus placebo in patients with post COVID-19 condition: a randomized, phase 2, crossover trial.

citations.label: Zeraatkar et al., 2024, BMJ
citations.title: Interventions for the management of long covid (post-covid condition): living systematic review.

products.name: Nicotinamide riboside and other NAD+ precursors
products.summary: In a 24-week double-blind trial, 58 people with Long COVID were randomized to nicotinamide riboside (2000 mg a day) or placebo first. It raised NAD+ levels within 5 weeks but did not improve cognition, fatigue, sleep or mood compared with placebo. Many people dropped out of the nicotinamide riboside group, and improvements seen within the group after 10 weeks were exploratory. A separate pilot study in 36 people gave NAD+ through skin patches together with low-dose naltrexone and reported improvements from baseline after 12 weeks; because both were given together, it cannot show the effect of NAD+ alone.
products.safety_interactions: In the randomized trial, one serious adverse event was reported and judged unrelated to the study treatment. In the pilot study, the NAD+ skin patches caused mild, short-lived skin irritation in 25% of people. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Nicotinamide riboside and NAD+ precursors
general_safety.short: Placebo-controlled trials of up to 8 weeks found adverse events no more common than with placebo; a meta-analysis of NMN trials agreed. Long-term safety is not established.

citations.label: Wu et al., 2025, EClinicalMedicine
citations.title: Effects of nicotinamide riboside on NAD+ levels, cognition, and symptom recovery in long-COVID: a randomized controlled trial.

citations.label: Isman et al., 2024, Brain Behav Immun Health
citations.title: Low-dose naltrexone and NAD+ for the treatment of patients with persistent fatigue symptoms after COVID-19.

products.name: Benfotiamine
products.summary: No randomized, observational or pilot studies of benfotiamine in people with Long COVID were found in a PubMed search on 23 November 2026. One registered single-arm study (NCT07745699) of a remote ketogenic diet and lifestyle programme for Long COVID included daily benfotiamine among several changes, so it cannot show the effect of benfotiamine alone, and no results from it are cited here. A different form of vitamin B1, thiamine, was tested with vitamins B6 and B12 in a randomized trial and made no difference (see B vitamins). Claims about benfotiamine in Long COVID rest on studies of other conditions or on laboratory reasoning.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials, because no Long COVID trials of benfotiamine were found.

products.name: Nattokinase
products.summary: No randomized, observational or pilot studies of nattokinase in people with Long COVID were found in a PubMed search on 23 November 2026, and no Long COVID trial of nattokinase was found on ClinicalTrials.gov. Claims about it in Long COVID rest on laboratory work and on studies of other conditions.
products.safety_interactions: Nattokinase is an enzyme taken for its clot-dissolving (fibrinolytic) activity. In a case report, a person taking aspirin had bleeding in the brain after taking nattokinase for 7 days, and the authors suggested it may raise the risk of brain bleeding in people with fragile small blood vessels in the brain who also take other anti-clotting (antithrombotic) medicines. A review of heart-health supplements noted that its use may be limited by bleeding risk or drug interactions. This is a particular concern for anyone taking anticoagulant or antiplatelet medicines; talk to a clinician first.

citations.label: Chang et al., 2008, Intern Med
citations.title: Cerebellar hemorrhage provoked by combined use of nattokinase and aspirin in a patient with cerebral microbleeds.

citations.label: Dobre et al., 2025, Int J Mol Sci
citations.title: Navigating the Effects of Anti-Atherosclerotic Supplements and Acknowledging Associated Bleeding Risks.

products.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
products.summary: One 12-week double-blind pilot trial in healthcare workers with Long COVID recruited 32 people, of whom 18 finished. Omega-3 did not significantly improve shortness of breath, cough, fatigue, or loss of taste or smell compared with placebo. The trial was designed to test feasibility and is too small to judge benefit.
products.safety_interactions: One person taking omega-3 and five taking placebo had adverse events; none were serious. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
general_safety.short: Linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation in cardiovascular trials, more so above 1 g/day; diarrhoea and altered taste were more likely than with placebo; bleeding findings are mixed.

citations.label: Sarkar et al., 2024, Cureus
citations.title: The Feasibility of Omega-3 Supplementation Compared to Placebo in the Management of Long COVID Symptoms Among Healthcare Workers: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
